note: Built after reading the cached classical texts (see sources/) and before writing annotation blocks. 'duplicates' lists later repetitions that were NOT given their own block. Sources inspected: Tabari, Ibn Kathir, Suyuti (Durr, via quran-tafsir.net text), Zamakhshari, Razi, Baydawi, Biqai, Qurtubi, Alusi (107:1 and 107:7 pages only), Ibn Atiyya (107:1 only), Wahidi (107:1-2 only; none for 3-7 on source page), Tabari 9:103 and 51:11, Qurtubi 67:30, Biqai 106:4 and 108:1, Maqayis (sahw, daʿ, yatm, manʿ, ḥaḍ). Not inspected as primary: Bukhari/Muslim/Abu Dawud/Tirmidhi/Ibn Majah text pages (sunnah.com blocked 403); hadith data come via Ibn Kathir/Suyuti/Qurtubi quotations plus a Muslim collection label on a secondary page.

supporting_sources: Qurtubi: Makkan per Ata, Jabir, one report of Ibn Abbas; Madani per Qatada and Ibn Abbas's other report
Suyuti: Ibn Mardawayh from Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr: revealed in Mecca
Alusi: jumhur Makkan; Abu Hayyan: Madani per Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Dahhak; Hibatullah al-Darir: half Mecca (al-As b. Wa'il) half Medina ('Abdullah b. Ubayy)
Ibn Atiyya: Makkan, 'no disagreement known to me'; Tha'labi says Madani
Zamakhshari: Makkiyya, qila Madaniyya
Baydawi: mukhtalaf fiha
contradicting_sources: Ibn Atiyya's 'no disagreement' vs Qurtubi/Alusi explicit disagreement

supporting_sources: Wahidi: Muqatil and Kalbi: al-As b. Wa'il al-Sahmi; Ibn Jurayj: Abu Sufyan b. Harb nahr jazur, orphan struck with staff
Razi: Ibn Jurayj Abu Sufyan; Muqatil al-As; Suddi al-Walid b. al-Mughira; Mawardi: Abu Jahl guardian-of-orphan story; Ibn Abbas: a hypocrite combining miserliness and riya
Qurtubi: Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas: al-As; Dahhak: 'Amr b. 'A'idh; Suddi: Walid; Abu Jahl; Dahhak/Ibn Abbas: a hypocrite
Baydawi: Abu Jahl or Abu Sufyan or Walid or a stingy hypocrite
Alusi adds Hibatullah split
contradicting_sources: Razi: view 2 = general (all deniers of the Day), not any one person

rows.claim: Asbab 107:7 (Ibn Mas'ud: Muslims borrowing from hypocrites)
supporting_sources: Suyuti attributing to Ibn Mardawayh (chain not seen)
Tabari: bi-thawab Allah wa-'iqabih; Ibn Abbas: bi-hukm Allah; Ibn Jurayj: bi'l-hisab
Ibn Kathir: al-ma'ad wa'l-jaza'
Qurtubi: bi'l-jaza' wa'l-hisab
Razi: three options; majority = hisab/jaza'; also Islam; din = khudu'
Baydawi: bi'l-jaza' aw al-Islam
Alusi: jaza' ('kama tadin tudan'); Mujahid hisab; Islam; Qur'an; Ibn Abbas hukm Allah
Ibn Atiyya: al-jaza' thawaban wa-'iqaban
Suyuti: Hasan: al-kafir; Ibn Jurayj hisab
rows.later_development: Razi gives reasons why the majority prefers jaza'; Alusi notes the options need not exclude each other
duplicates: Kathir/Qurtubi/Ibn Atiyya repeat the jaza'/hisab reading

supporting_sources: Tabari: yadfa' haqqahu wa-yazlimuh (Ibn Abbas: yadfa' haqq al-yatim); Mujahid: yadfa'uh fa-la yut'imuh; Qatada, Dahhak: yaqhar(uh) wa-yazlim; Sufyan: yadfa'uh
Suyuti: Ibn Abbas to Nafi' b. al-Azraq with Abu Talib verse (via al-Tusti); Muhammad b. Ka'b yadfa'uh; Qatada yazlimuh
Zamakhshari: dafa' 'anif bi-jafwa wa-adha
Razi: three layers (deprive of right; withhold mu'asat; scold/hit/slight); shadhdh yada'; 'yad'u'; tashdid = habit
Qurtubi: yadfa'; mutaqarib
Kathir: yaqhar wa-yazlim haqqah wa-la yut'im
rows.later_development: Razi's habit/tashdid point and shadhdh readings widen the range
rows.novelty_status: explicit (core); base's da'da'a/di'a' network: none found

supporting_sources: Tabari: la yahuththu ghayrahu
Zamakhshari: la yab'athu ahlahu
Razi: two readings: does not urge himself / does not urge others; idafa shows food is the miskin's due
Baydawi: ahlahu wa-ghayrahum
Biqai: yahuththu nafsahu wa-ahlahu wa-la ghayrahum; ihtibak
Qurtubi: la ya'muru; blame is not general: excludes those who cannot
Kathir: miskin = al-faqir alladhi la shay'a lahu
rows.novelty_status: explicit (range); base hadd/hadid network: building block

supporting_sources: Tabari: wayl = a valley flowing with pus of Jahannam, for hypocrites who pray
Kathir: musallin = those who belong to ahl al-salat and are committed to it; Ibn Abbas and others: hypocrites
Razi: wayl for serious crime (cf. 83:1); fa- = sababiyya; al-mu'tamad: wayl for hypocrite-musallin; Shafi'i point on kuffar and furu'
Zamakhshari/Baydawi: fa- jaza'iyya; musallin put in place of the pronoun; jins
Biqai: wayl = strongest sign of contempt; wasf for generalisation
Alusi/Abu Hayyan: mukallafun bi'l-salat even kuffar; hypocrite identification due to 'alladhina hum yura'un'
Qurtubi: wayl = 'adhab
contradicting_sources: hypocrite-only (Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Malik via Alusi/Tabari) vs inclusive (Razi's other answers, Alusi/Abu Hayyan)
rows.novelty_status: ṣalā-fire network: no parallel found; wayl-as-valley-in-Jahannam = building block

supporting_sources: Tabari: three early groups: delay beyond time (Sa'd, Mus'ab, Masruq, Abu l-Duha, Ibn Abbas via Abu Jamra, Ibn Abza, Muslim b. Subayh); leaving (Ibn Abbas, Mujahid); heedless/trifling (Mujahid lahun, Qatada ghafilun/la yubali, Ibn Zayd 'prayer is not their concern'); Tabari: sahw covers all of these
Kathir: lafz covers leaving, delaying out of time, delaying from first time, unconditional performance, khushu'; each gets a share
Zamakhshari: 'an = sahw tark/qillat iltifat (munafiqun, fussaq); fi = waswasa, hadith nafs (almost every Muslim; the Prophet himself); Anas: 'al-hamdu lillah that He did not say fi'
Razi: Ibn Abbas via 'Ata: if fi, the threat would be on believers; Razi: 'an-sahw is the act of the kafir, fi-sahw of the mu'min
Qurtubi: Abu l-'Aliya: not at their times, not completing ruku'/sujud; Ibrahim: turns his head; Qutrub: neither recites nor remembers God; Ibn Abbas: neither hopes reward nor fears punishment
Suyuti: Abu l-'Aliya (does not know whether even or odd), Hasan: 'meaning sahw about its time until it passes'
Biqai: 'an not fi = tadyi'; Ibn Mas'ud 'lahun'
Baydawi: ghafilun ghayr mubalin
Tabari 51:11 (usage: sahun fi ghamra = lahun)
contradicting_sources: Razi: calls the 'sahw = leaving' sense weak as an explanation because the verse affirms they pray
Ata's name: Tabari and Ibn Kathir 'Ata b. Dinar'; Suyuti text 'Ata b. Yasar' (discrepancy to note)
rows.hadith_relation: Sa'd (marfu'/mawquf), Abu Barza (weak), Muslim (hypocrite's prayer; thematic)
rows.novelty_status: explicit (the 'an/fi point); base's 'outside the prayer while praying' image = one live branch
duplicates: Qurtubi repeats Zamakhshari's an/fi passage verbatim (attributed); Ibn Kathir repeats Tabari's Sa'd/Abu Barza and adds Bayhaqi/Hakim

rows.claim: Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas report on sahun
supporting_sources: Tabari: Mus'ab asked his father (mawquf) and a marfu' route via Mus'ab; Ibn Kathir: marfu' weak (Bayhaqi), mawquf asahh (Bayhaqi, Hakim); Suyuti: 'al-mawquf asahh' (Hakim, Bayhaqi); Qurtubi cites marfu' with 'tahawunan bi-ha'
Tabari; Ibn Kathir: Jabir al-Ju'fi weak, shaykh unnamed; Suyuti: 'bi-sanad da'if'
Zamakhshari/Razi: mufa'ala from ira'a; the show-er shows his work and they show him praise; displaying obligatory acts is not riya' ('wa-la ghumma fi fara'id Allah'); riya' hidden like a black ant
Tabari: they pray for people to see, so believers refrain from shedding their blood and enslaving their children (hypocrites)
Qurtubi: four forms of riya' (Ibn al-'Arabi)
Suyuti: Ali: yura'un bi-salatihim
Kathir: Ahmad: 'man samma'a'; Abu Ya'la/Tirmidhi: two rewards (gharib); Tabarani: valley for al-mura'in
rows.novelty_status: mir'at/mirror: none found; mutual seeing: explicit (mufa'ala)

supporting_sources: Tabari: zakat (Ali via Mujahid and via Abu Salih, Ibn Umar, Hasan, Qatada, Said b. Jubayr, Ibn al-Hanafiyya, Dahhak, Ibn Zayd); household items (Ibn Mas'ud via Abu l-'Ubaydayn, via Ibrahim, via Abu Wa'il; 'saḥabat Muhammad'; Ibn Abbas via Mujahid and Said b. Jubayr: 'ariya, mata' al-bayt; Ikrima); ma'ruf (Muhammad b. Ka'b); mal in Qurashi (Said b. al-Musayyab, Zuhri); Ibn Abbas: people differ: zakat, ta'a, 'ariya; Ibn Abbas: 'its people have not come yet' (Layth); Tabari's own tarjih: general, covers both loans and obligatory rights; language: water from cloud, Ashʿa and another verse, 'Ubayd al-Ra'i verse (ta'a/zakat)

Qurtubi: 12 views (zakat; mal; household goods; every benefit in jahiliyya and ta'a/zakat in Islam; 'ariya; ma'ruf; water and pasture; water; manʿ al-haqq (Ibn Umar); small things; obedience; what is not permitted to refuse: water, salt, fire (A'isha, Ibn Majah, 'isnad has softness')

Razi: 4 views; zakat; household items (most mufassirs; fa'ul from ma'n, small); water (Fara'); obedience (rudh ba'iraka hatta tu'tiyaka al-ma'un); prefers any easy act of obedience; link with 'yura'un': 'prayer is for Me, ma'un for the creatures'
Ibn Kathir: Ikrima: ra's al-ma'un zakat al-mal, adnahu al-munkhul wa'l-dalw wa'l-ibra; Ibn Kathir: this covers all views; all return to withholding assistance
Zamakhshari: zakat; Ibn Mas'ud household; A'isha water/fire/salt; withholding may be forbidden if borrowed from necessity, reprehensible in muruwwa otherwise
Baydawi: zakat or what is customarily lent
Alusi: etymologies (ma'n small; ma'una with alif for ha; maf'ul of a'ana; metathesis); Abu 'Ubayd, Zajjaj, Mubarrad: jahiliyya every benefit, Islam ta'a
Biqai: haqq al-amwal and the small things; Qutrub ma'n = ma'ruf; Abu 'Ubayda jahiliyya 'ata'/manfa'a, Islam zakat

Suyuti: many reports; Ibn Mardawayh: Ibn Mas'ud asbab; Qurra b. Dahmus (Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh); Ali via Ibn Qani'; al-Harith b. Shurayh (Bawardi); Umm 'Atiyya (Tabarani, weak); Abu Hurayra (Abu Nu'aym, Daylami, Ibn 'Asakir)
contradicting_sources: Razi says household items are the view of 'most mufassirs'; Tabari's chains lean heavily to zakat by count (counted by reports, not weighted)
rows.hadith_relation: Qurra b. Dahmus (Ibn Kathir: gharib jiddan, raf' munkar, unknown in isnad); Ali via Ibn Qani' (Suyuti); A'isha (Qurtubi); Ibn Mas'ud 'ariyat al-dalw wa'l-qidr (Abu Dawud, Nasa'i per Ibn Kathir)
rows.historical_context: household lending of fa's, qidr, dalw, mizan, munkhul, ibra, miqdaha (fire-striker); neighbours baking in one's tannur (Razi); 'ariya = return of the item (Ibn Kathir)
duplicates: Ibn Kathir repeats Tabari's chains; Alusi/Qurtubi repeat Razi's list; Suyuti collects the same reports with other collectors

supporting_sources: Biqai 107:7 closing: 'wa-kama iltaqa akhiruha bi-awwaliha...'; 107:7: those who deny trivial things are fit to be denied the Kawthar; 107:1 and Ibn al-Zubayr (via Biqai) on 100-105; Quraysh (106:4 end: akhiruha 'illa li-awwaliha); Biqai 108:1: Kawthar opens with al-'ata' against 107's manʿ; Razi closing prayer: next surah describes Muhammad
rows.novelty_status: explicit for end-meets-beginning (Biqai); base's specific objects (din and ma'un meet in ta'a): building blocks

supporting_sources: Zamakhshari/Razi/Baydawi: 'arayta without hamza (Zajjaj: not the preferred form); Ibn Mas'ud 'ara'aytaka; Alusi: Kisa'i drops hamza; Ibn Atiyya: Abu 'Amr hamz with khilaf, Nafi' not
Tabari: 'Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud): yukadhdhibu al-din (no ba')
Zamakhshari/Razi/Baydawi: yada' (leaves) and Razi yad'u
Ibn Mas'ud: lahun (Suyuti: Ibn al-Anbari, Bayhaqi, Khatib; Zamakhshari; Qurtubi; Biqai)
